skills.name: test-driven-development
skills.purpose: Force a failing test to exist before any production code is written, for features and bugfixes alike.
skills.mechanism: Iron Law hard gate ("NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST" — code written first must be deleted, not adapted) driving a RED-GREEN-REFACTOR loop with mandatory watch-it-fail and watch-it-pass verification steps; bulletproofed by a rationalization table, red-flags list, and completion checklist, with reference file writing-good-tests.md adding two pre-write gate functions ("name the break this test catches", mock-at-the-right-level) plus a mutation check.
skills.invocation: Model-invoked via trigger-only description; also chained by name as REQUIRED background from systematic-debugging and writing-skills.

skills.name: systematic-debugging
skills.purpose: Force root-cause investigation before any fix is proposed for any bug, failure, or unexpected behavior.
skills.mechanism: Four sequential gated phases (root-cause investigation → pattern analysis vs working examples → single-hypothesis minimal test → test-first fix), with a quantified circuit breaker: 3+ failed fixes means stop and question the architecture with the human; hardened by red-flags/rationalization tables and human-signal cues ("stop guessing"). Ships reference techniques (root-cause-tracing.md: trace bad values up the call chain and fix at source; defense-in-depth.md: validate at every layer; condition-based-waiting.md: poll for conditions not timeouts), a find-polluter.sh bisection script, and its own test fixtures (test-academic.md, test-pressure-1/2/3.md) plus a CREATION-LOG.md documenting how the skill was extracted and bulletproofed.
skills.invocation: Model-invoked on any bug/test failure, explicitly including under time pressure; chains by name to test-driven-development and verification-before-completion in Phase 4.

skills.name: verification-before-completion
skills.purpose: Forbid any success or completion claim without fresh verification evidence in the same message.
skills.mechanism: Five-step gate function (identify the proving command → run it fully → read full output → check it confirms the claim → only then claim, with evidence), a claim→required-evidence mapping table (tests, build, bug fixed, agent-reported success all need independent proof), and a ban on satisfaction phrases and paraphrased success wording before verification.
skills.invocation: Model-invoked before any completion/success claim, commit, or PR; chained by name from systematic-debugging and finishing workflows.

skills.name: requesting-code-review
skills.purpose: Dispatch a fresh-context subagent reviewer to check completed work against its plan before issues cascade.
skills.mechanism: Fills the code-reviewer.md prompt template (description, plan/requirements, base+head SHAs, read-only rules) and dispatches a general-purpose subagent that never sees session history — only crafted context; reviewer must return a fixed contract: Strengths, issues tiered Critical/Important/Minor with file:line and why-it-matters, Recommendations, and an explicit ready-to-merge verdict; caller must fix Critical immediately and Important before proceeding, and may push back with reasoning.
skills.invocation: Model-invoked; mandatory after each task in subagent-driven development, after major features, and before merge.

skills.name: receiving-code-review
skills.purpose: Replace performative agreement or blind implementation of review feedback with technical verification.
skills.mechanism: Six-step response pattern (read → restate → verify against codebase reality → evaluate → respond or push back → implement one item at a time with tests); forbids "You're absolutely right!"/gratitude phrases, requires clarifying all unclear items before implementing any, applies source-specific trust (partner trusted, external reviewers verified, YAGNI grep-check for suggested features), and prescribes factual correction when your pushback was wrong.
skills.invocation: Model-invoked whenever review feedback arrives, especially when it seems unclear or questionable.

skills.name: finishing-a-development-branch
skills.purpose: Govern how completed, green-tested work gets integrated, kept, or (only on explicit request) discarded.
skills.mechanism: Gates on a fresh full-suite pass, detects environment (normal repo vs worktree vs detached HEAD) to pick a fixed verbatim options menu (merge locally / push+PR / keep as-is; discard exists only as a response to an explicit request and requires the literally typed word "discard"), confirms the base branch before merging, re-runs tests on the merged result, and cleans up only worktrees under self-owned paths (.worktrees//worktrees/); rationalization table blocks stale-green-run and assumed-intent shortcuts.
skills.invocation: Model-invoked at implementation completion; announces itself at start; integration choice always waits for the human.

skills.name: using-git-worktrees
skills.purpose: Ensure feature work happens in an isolated workspace with a verified clean baseline.
skills.mechanism: Detect-before-create ordering: check whether already isolated (GIT_DIR vs GIT_COMMON with a submodule guard), prefer the harness's native worktree tool over manual git worktree (manual creates "phantom state"), verify the worktree directory is gitignored before creating, then run project setup and baseline tests so later failures are unambiguous.
skills.invocation: Model-invoked at feature start or before executing plans; announces itself; asks user consent unless a preference is already declared.

skills.name: writing-skills
skills.purpose: Apply TDD to process documentation itself: no skill is written or edited without first watching an agent fail without it.
skills.mechanism: RED-GREEN-REFACTOR with subagent pressure scenarios (RED: baseline runs without the skill, rationalizations captured verbatim; GREEN: minimal skill addressing those exact failures; REFACTOR: close each new loophole with explicit negations, rationalization-table entries, and red flags), plus a "match the form to the failure" taxonomy (prohibitions for discipline violations, positive recipes for wrong-shaped output, structural slots for omissions, observable-predicate conditionals), cheap micro-tests with a no-guidance control and 5+ reps before full scenarios, and Skill Discovery Optimization rules (description = triggering conditions only, never a workflow summary; keyword coverage; token budgets). References: testing-skills-with-subagents.md (pressure types — time/sunk cost/authority/exhaustion/social — forced A/B/C choices, meta-testing "how should the skill have been written?"), persuasion-principles.md (Cialdini/Meincke: authority+commitment+social proof for discipline skills, never liking), anthropic-best-practices.md (progressive disclosure, naming, feedback-loop checklists), graphviz-conventions.dot + render-graphs.js (flowchart DSL and SVG renderer), examples/CLAUDE_MD_TESTING.md (worked variant-testing campaign).
skills.invocation: Model-invoked when creating or editing any skill; requires test-driven-development as named background; Iron Law applies to edits as well as new skills.

patterns: Iron Laws: one absolute bright-line gate per skill ("NO X WITHOUT Y FIRST") prefaced by "violating the letter is violating the spirit" to pre-empt spirit-vs-letter negotiation.
Gate functions: short numbered pre-claim checklists that must execute before any status claim — evidence before assertion, with a claim→required-evidence mapping table.

Rationalization tables + red-flag lists: harvest the exact excuses agents produce under pressure (verbatim) and pair each with a counter; red flags act as self-check tripwires that trigger stop-and-restart.

Phase gating with a quantified escalation threshold: sequential phases that cannot be skipped, plus a circuit breaker (3 failed attempts → question the architecture, consult the human) that converts repeated failure into a strategy review.

Fresh-context second opinion: dispatch a reviewer subagent with precisely crafted context (never session history) and a fixed output contract — tiered severity, file:line specificity, explicit verdict.

Test the docs like code: RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for guidance — baseline an agent failing without the document, write minimal guidance against those observed failures, close loopholes iteratively; meta-test by asking the violator how the doc should have been written.

Pressure-scenario testing: forced A/B/C choices combining 3+ pressures (time, sunk cost, authority, exhaustion, social) as the test fixture format for discipline rules; academic quizzes only verify comprehension, not compliance.

Match the form to the failure: prohibitions only for knowing-violation failures; positive recipes/contracts for wrong-shaped output; structural required-slots for omissions; conditionals keyed to observable predicates — no nuance clauses ever.
Fixed verbatim menus for irreversible decisions, with destructive paths reachable only via explicit request plus an exact typed confirmation token.
Detect-before-create and prefer-native: check whether the desired state already exists, use the harness's own tools over manual equivalents, and only clean up artifacts under self-owned paths.
Verify a clean baseline before starting work so later failures are attributable to the work itself.
Description = trigger only: metadata says when to load, never what the process is, so agents cannot shortcut the body by following the summary.

Cross-reference companion skills by name with explicit REQUIRED markers; never force-load, preserving progressive disclosure (SKILL.md core + reference files loaded on demand, token budgets on frequently-loaded docs).
Defense-in-depth: after fixing at the root cause, add validation at every layer the bad data passes through so the failure becomes structurally impossible.
Commitment devices: skills announce themselves at start; checklists become tracked todos; forced explicit choices — leveraging authority/commitment/social-proof persuasion deliberately and ethically.
Anti-sycophancy protocol for incoming feedback: verify against reality before implementing, push back with evidence, ban performative agreement phrases.
Bisection tooling for pollution: a script that runs units one-by-one to isolate which one corrupts shared state.
knowledgeWorkAnalogs: Claim-first research (TDD analog): state the claim and what evidence would falsify it before drafting prose; verify the source actually supports it (watch the claim "fail" against a null source) before the sentence enters the draft — no claim without a checked citation first.

Systematic error-tracing for facts (debugging analog): when a fact looks wrong, trace the citation chain back to the primary source and fix the source note, not the manuscript sentence; after fixing, add defense-in-depth checks at capture, synthesis, citation, and publication layers of the note pipeline.

Three-strikes thesis rule: if three reframings of an argument each fail or spawn new contradictions, stop patching paragraphs and question the outline/thesis itself with the human before attempt four.

Verification-before-submission gate: before claiming a report/essay/analysis is "done," run explicit checks with evidence — every citation resolves, every number recomputed from raw data, every quote diffed against the original — and state completion only with that evidence in hand.

Fresh-context draft reviewer: dispatch a subagent given only the brief, the requirements, and the draft delta (never the writing-session history) that must return Strengths, Critical/Important/Minor issues with location and why-it-matters, and an explicit ready-to-publish verdict.

Editorial-feedback reception protocol: restate each comment, verify it against the manuscript and sources, push back with evidence when the editor lacks context, clarify all unclear comments before implementing any, and implement one at a time — no "great point!" performance.

Finishing-a-draft menu: on completion present a fixed menu (merge into the vault/publication, send for review, park as-is); deleting a draft requires the human's explicit request plus a typed confirmation, and cleanup touches only drafts in the system's own drafts folder.

Draft isolation with baseline check (worktree analog): revise in a copy/branch of a living note or document, first verifying the current vault is healthy (links resolve, index builds) so post-edit breakage is attributable to the revision.

Rationalization tables for scholarly shortcuts: enumerate the exact excuses ("the abstract is enough," "a secondary source is fine," "I remember this statistic," "I'll add citations after drafting") each paired with a counter, plus a red-flags list that triggers stop-and-verify.

Pressure-test your PKM/writing guidelines before adopting them: run a subagent on a tempting scenario without the guideline (baseline), write the minimal guideline against the observed failure, and iterate until it holds under combined deadline+sunk-cost+authority pressure.
Mutation check for arguments: mentally negate each premise of a finished piece; if no cited source or check would catch the negation, that claim is unprotected and needs evidence or removal.
Bisection for a corrupted knowledge base: when links/tags/indexes break after bulk imports, replay recent note batches one-by-one to isolate the polluting import.
Condition-based waiting analog for research workflows: gate next steps on observable conditions ("reply received," "dataset published," "embargo lifted") rather than arbitrary elapsed-time guesses.
Trigger-only descriptions for PKM templates and prompts: metadata says when to open a template, never summarizes its steps, so the user/agent reads the actual checklist instead of a lossy summary.
